meta.title: Half a Batch of Cookies
meta.textType: functional: a recipe in steps with a maths task, made at home

paragraphs: On Thursday, February eighteenth, Teacher Kim gave the Explorers a math task. Each child had to halve a recipe card from Chef Lucy's cooking class. The card made twelve cookies, but the new card had to make six. That evening, Lily and Tom worked in the kitchen at home. Tom came to help, because he liked cookies. Lily put two bowls, a small scale, and the recipe card on the counter. Pip sat on the floor and looked up at the counter. "Half of twelve is six," said Lily. She wrote the numbers on a notepad.

The card for twelve cookies had five ingredients. It listed two hundred grams of flour and one hundred grams of sugar. It listed one hundred grams of coconut and eighty grams of butter. The last ingredient was one egg. Lily drew a second column on the card for six cookies. She wrote one hundred grams of flour and fifty grams of sugar. Then she wrote fifty grams of coconut and forty grams of butter. "You cannot use half an egg!" said Tom. "We beat the egg, and then we use half," said Lily. Tom laughed and nodded.

Lily wrote the steps in order on the new card, and Tom read the first one. "First, take the butter from the refrigerator." Lily took two wooden spoons from a drawer. "Next, mix the butter and the sugar in a bowl," read Tom. He held the bowl with his left hand and stirred with his right hand. "Then add half of the beaten egg, the flour, and the coconut," read Lily. Lily weighed each ingredient on the scale and put it in the bowl. Dad came into the kitchen and turned on the oven. Pip sat in front of the oven and watched the door.

"After that, make six balls and put them on a tray," read Lily. The dough was soft, and it smelled of coconut. Lily made six round balls with her hands. Dad watched while Tom put the tray inside. "Finally, bake the balls for twelve minutes and wait," read Tom. "Is twelve minutes a long time?" he asked. "It is, when the kitchen smells so good," said Lily. Waiting was the hardest step of all.

After twelve minutes, Dad took the tray out of the oven. The six cookies were golden and tasty. Tom ate one, and Lily ate one. "Is a half recipe really half the work?" asked Tom. "No, but it is half the cookies, and that is enough," said Lily. Pip looked at the tray with big eyes, but he got only a look. Lily put the new card in her bag for Friday.
